claims.title: The manager's ranking tracks the spot
claims.claim: The manager's ranking is consistent, but it tracks the spot, not the machine. Jan–Apr house win follows the spot's expected play (ρ 0.61), not machine effect (ρ 0.10). Our ranking is the one that predicts which machines underperform their spot (ρ 0.58 vs. 0.05).
claims.source: outputs/metrics.json → persistence_compare (pipeline/verdicts.py, model_machine.py): Spearman ρ of Jan–Apr rankings vs. May–Jun outcomes, 2,000 bootstrap resamples of machines
claims.result: Jan–Apr house win vs. spot expectation ρ 0.61, vs. machine effect ρ 0.10 (n 309). Predicting May–Jun machine effect: ours ρ 0.58 [0.51, 0.64], manager ρ 0.05 [-0.05, 0.14].
claims.alternative: The manager's ranking is not noise: it predicts May–Jun house win (ρ 0.67) while ours does not (ρ -0.01). That is what a spot-driven ranking should do, so both readings were tested on the same holdout.
claims.limitation: Machine effect is our own model's estimate (play vs. spot expectation); synthetic data, one property.

claims.title: Half the manager's list pays back more by design
claims.claim: 5 of the manager's 10 are configured at 5% expected hold, the floor's lowest setting (25 of 310 machines; floor median 10%). At the median setting the same play would carry about 2× the theo.
claims.source: outputs/metrics.json → low_hold (pipeline/alternatives.py): game_math configured RTP per machine, hypergeometric test
claims.result: Hypergeometric p = 0.0004; theo $119.9k vs. $239.9k at the median setting.
claims.alternative: Low theo could be unlucky variance instead of setting: observed hold on these 5 is 2.4%–5.4%, around the 5% setting, so the low take is game math.
claims.limitation: Low hold is a design choice that may attract play; this does not say those machines should be changed.

claims.title: Play probably follows the spot, on thin evidence
claims.claim: Across the 4 machines that moved, the pooled slope of play on spot is 0.90 [0.44, 1.07] against the model and 1.23 [0.10, 1.38] against bank peers.
claims.source: outputs/metrics.json → alternatives.moved (pipeline/alternatives.py): log play change vs. log spot change, ≥ 14 days each side, leave-one-out
claims.alternative: One move could drive the estimate: dropping M-1152 lowers the peer slope to 0.52, near the 0.5 line. The 0.5 decision threshold was set after seeing these estimates, so it is not pre-registered.
claims.limitation: Only 4 moves; the move test in the plan exists to settle this.

claims.title: Our weak-machine ranking persists out of sample
claims.claim: Of our bottom 10 machines by Jan–Apr effect, 4 are still in the bottom 10 in May–Jun; rank correlation 0.58.
claims.alternative: Persistence could come from the spot, not the machine: effect is play divided by the spot expectation, so a pure spot ranking scores ρ ≈ 0 on it (the manager's list: 0.05).
claims.limitation: Two months of holdout; 4 of 10 also means 6 of 10 moved out of the bottom.

claims.title: None of the manager's 10 is on our weak list
claims.claim: Of 310 machines over Jan–Jun, 60 are truly weak, 43 are held back by their spot, 18 by luck and 1 needs an inspection; none of the manager's 10 is on our list.
claims.alternative: The count of weak machines depends on the play model: before themes and bet range were added it was 136, after 60; the overlap with the manager's list was 2 before and 0 after.
claims.limitation: Thresholds (shrunk upper bound < 1, luck |z|) are conventions, not estimated.

claims.title: M-1158 holds far below its setting
claims.claim: M-1158 held 3.0% against a configured 10.0% over Jan–Jun.
claims.source: machine_scorecard.parquet → hold_obs, hold_expected, hold_gap_z, z_half1/2, bh_reject (pipeline/holdgap.py)
claims.result: z = -4.6; -2.9 and -3.5 in each half; survives 10% FDR across 310 machines. 1 machine flagged.
claims.alternative: Bad luck: the same shortfall in both halves makes chance unlikely. A different paytable fits better (G-VID95, z -1.3), so the next step is to inspect and verify the configuration.
claims.limitation: Hold variance is information, not a finding: verification may confirm a configuration difference or find nothing.

claims.title: Volatility does not explain the manager's list
claims.claim: 4 of the manager's 10 are high volatility vs. 35% of the floor.
claims.alternative: This was the alternative: high-volatility games swing more and could look weak by chance. Not supported.
claims.limitation: Ten machines give little power; a modest volatility effect cannot be ruled out.

claims.title: The manager's machines are not under-tracked
claims.claim: Carded share of coin-in on the manager's 10 is 66.0% vs. 65.8% on the rest.
claims.alternative: Low earners could be machines where guests skip the card, so tracked play understates them. The shares match.
claims.limitation: Carded share only covers tracked play; uncarded behavior is not observed.

claims.title: Daily floor coin-in is forecastable from weekday and events
claims.claim: On the May–Jun holdout (2025-05-01 to 2025-06-30), the weekday × event model misses daily coin-in by $63.9k on average (WAPE 4.7%).
claims.source: outputs/forecast_holdout.parquet; metrics.json → model2 (pipeline/model_floor.py), trained Jan–Apr only
claims.result: MAE $63.9k vs. $68.7k weekday-only and $218.3k flat mean (71% better). Event uplift ×1.07 from 20 training event days.
claims.alternative: A flat mean or weekday-only model could do as well; both were scored on the same holdout.
claims.limitation: Only 3 event days in the holdout; bias $45.1k/day (underforecast).

claims.title: Sats bring in 1.64× a Tue's coin-in
claims.claim: Jan–Apr mean daily coin-in is $1.82M on Sat vs. $1.11M on Tue.
claims.source: metrics.json → model2.weekday_mean (machine_day, gaming date 6 a.m. boundary)
claims.alternative: Events could create the pattern; event-day uplift is only ×1.07, too small to produce the weekday gap.
claims.limitation: Four months; summer patterns may differ.

claims.title: Back Forty lost traffic while its walkway was closed
claims.claim: Z-B40's share of floor door-counter traffic fell from 3.86% to 2.78% while walkway W-ENT-B40 was closed for renovation (Mar 3 – Apr 7).
claims.source: web/public/data/demand.json → closures (pipeline/demand.py; traffic with offline hours masked and filled)
claims.result: Z-ENT share 19.1% → 16.7% over the same days.
claims.alternative: A seasonal dip could explain it; shares are relative to floor traffic, so floor-wide swings cancel.
claims.limitation: One closure; shares are descriptive, not a controlled comparison. Signage lift in the plan is an assumption.

claims.title: Grave shift waits longest for a technician
claims.claim: Downtime cost about $93.9k of theo over Jan–Jun (5,021 unavailable hours, 1,207 fault tickets). Grave-shift tickets wait 1.96 h for a technician vs. 0.87 h on day and swing.
claims.result: Lost theo range $79.7k–$106.1k. Grave is rostered with 1 technician (actual 1.00) vs. 2 on swing.
claims.alternative: Ticket volume could cause the waits, but grave has the fewest tickets (day 327, swing 577, grave 303), so the longer wait lines up with its single rostered technician, not load.
claims.limitation: Lost theo assumes the machine would have played at its own same-weekday rate; night tickets are an upper estimate.

claims.title: A small share of carded players carries most theo
claims.claim: The top 10% of carded players produce 66% of their theo; the top 1%, 23% (Gini 0.75).
claims.alternative: Concentration could just be the tier mix: within tiers it is weaker (top 10% share Base 63%, Gold 30%, Platinum 33%), so much of it is between tiers.
claims.limitation: Carded play only. Not a basis for targeting heavy losers.

claims.title: Comp reinvestment stepped up in late April
claims.claim: Weekly comp cost ÷ theo moved from 1.20% to 1.30% the week of 2025-04-21 (90% CI 2025-04-14 to 2025-04-28).
claims.source: loyalty_ledger economic cost ÷ sessions theo by full week → comps.json (pipeline/comps.py: SSE split, moving-block bootstrap)
claims.result: Effect +0.10 pts [+0.08, +0.13]; no-break null p = 0.04. Points per $ redeemed 13.1 → 6.0 the week of 2025-04-28.
claims.alternative: A shift in who plays could raise reinvestment; earn rate (points per $ wagered) and cost per $ of face are flat, so the step tracks the redemption price.
claims.limitation: The ledger does not record why the redemption price changed; one split is assumed.

claims.title: Comps are counted once
claims.claim: Comped F&B cost of goods ($190.7k) equals the ledger's economic comp cost ($190.7k), so comps are counted in cogs only.
claims.alternative: Adding ledger cost to cogs would double-count; tested in tests/test_money_math.py and test_players_comps.py.
claims.limitation: Face value is not cost; reinvestment uses economic cost.

claims.title: The plan buys a controlled move test
claims.claim: Swap 3 of our low-effect machines in busier spots with 3 of the manager's quiet-spot machines ($10.8k), each against a matched unmoved control.
claims.result: Planned 90% interval on the slope ±0.14; information value $9.2k; theo + information $12.6k vs. $2.0k for A-REPLACE-LEASE, which it replaces.
claims.alternative: With the wider peer-calibrated variation (±0.29) information value is $8.3k and the test is still included.
claims.limitation: Information value depends on the follow-on decision (90-day lease replacement) and its assumed new-title effect.

claims.title: The recommended plan holds under most changes
claims.claim: Spend $19.5k on A-INSPECT + A-WAYFINDING + A-MOVE-MACHINE and keep $80.5k; the same plan wins in 19 of 21 sensitivity scenarios.
claims.source: budget.json → recommended, sensitivity (pipeline/budget.py best_plan, sensitivity; tests/test_budget.py)
claims.result: Exhaustive search agrees with the plan; expected theo $7.1k–$36.0k within 30 days.
claims.alternative: Every line at its low end, or inspection worth $0, drops inspection from the plan; nothing else changes the pick.
claims.limitation: Signage lift (2–10%) and new-title effects are assumptions, not estimates.

approved: The manager's ranking is consistent, but it tracks the spot, not the machine. Jan–Apr house win follows the spot's expected play (ρ 0.61), not machine effect (ρ 0.10). Our ranking is the one that predicts which machines underperform their spot (ρ 0.58 vs. 0.05).
